claims.object_text: Q/R site editing occurs with ~99% efficiency; majority of AMPARs contain GluA2(R)
claims.quote: RNA editing at the Q/R site of GluA2 occurs with ~99% efficiency in the healthy brain, so that the majority of AMPARs contain GluA2(R) instead of the exonically encoded GluA2(Q).

claims.object_text: Reduced Q/R site editing increases AMPA receptor calcium permeability
claims.quote: Reduced Q/R site editing infcreases AMPA receptor calcium permeability and leads to dendritic spine loss, neurodegeneration, seizures and learning impairments.

claims.object_text: dendritic spine loss; neurodegeneration; seizures; learning impairments
claims.quote: Reduced Q/R site editing infcreases AMPA receptor calcium permeability and leads to dendritic spine loss, neurodegeneration, seizures and learning impairments.

claims.object_text: GluA2 Q/R site editing is impaired in Alzheimer's disease
claims.quote: GluA2 Q/R site editing is impaired in Alzheimer's disease (AD)

claims.object_text: inhibiting expression of unedited GluA2(Q) while maintaining GluA2(R) expression as a strategy to prevent synapse loss and neurodegeneration in AD
claims.quote: inhibiting expression of unedited GluA2(Q), while maintaining expression of GluA2(R), may be a novel strategy of preventing synapse loss and neurodegeneration in AD.

claims.object_text: mouse engineered with arginine codon (CGG) at position 607 of Gria2
claims.quote: We engineered mice with the 'edited' arginine codon (CGG) in place of the unedited glutamine codon (CAG) at position 607 of the Gria2 gene.

claims.object_text: Gria2-edited mice crossbred with the J20 mouse model of AD
claims.quote: We crossbred this line with the J20 mouse model of AD and conducted anatomical, electrophysiological and behavioural assays to determine the impact of eliminating unedited GluA2(Q) expression on AD-related phenotypes.

claims.object_text: prevention of dendritic spine loss and hippocampal CA1 neurodegeneration in AD mice
claims.quote: Eliminating unedited GluA2(Q) expression in AD mice prevented dendritic spine loss and hippocampal CA1 neurodegeneration as well as improved working and reference memory in the radial arm maze.

claims.object_text: improved working and reference memory in radial arm maze
claims.quote: Eliminating unedited GluA2(Q) expression in AD mice prevented dendritic spine loss and hippocampal CA1 neurodegeneration as well as improved working and reference memory in the radial arm maze.

claims.object_text: phenotypic improvements occurred independently of Aβ pathology and ongoing seizure susceptibility
claims.quote: These phenotypes were improved independently of Aβ pathology and ongoing seizure susceptibility.

claims.object_text: increased spine density in non-AD mice with exonically encoded GluA2(R)
claims.quote: Surprisingly, our data also revealed increased spine density in non-AD mice with exonically encoded GluA2(R) as compared to their wild-type littermates, suggesting an unexpected and previously unknown role for unedited GluA2(Q) in regulating dendritic spines.

claims.object_text: Q/R editing site may act as an epigenetic switch regulating dendritic spines, neurodegeneration and memory deficits in AD
claims.quote: The Q/R editing site of the AMPA receptor subunit GluA2 may act as an epigenetic switch that regulates dendritic spines, neurodegeneration and memory deficits in AD.
